name: Shatrughna
role: Rama's youngest brother, a ruler of Mathura
summary: In the Valmiki Ramayana, Shatrughna is the twin of Lakshmana and the youngest of Dasharatha's four sons. A late chapter credits him with defeating Lavana and settling Mathura.
about: Shatrughna is the youngest son of King Dasharatha, born to Sumitra with his twin Lakshmana in the Valmiki Ramayana. His name means killer of enemies. Some tellings say he was close to Bharata and stayed in Ayodhya to run the state while Bharata lived at Nandigrama. He married Shrutakirti. The Uttara Kanda tells how he defeated Lavana, the son of Madhu, and founded the city that later became Mathura. Puranic tradition links him to the Sudarshana chakra. Temples to him are rare, but Kerala keeps one at Payammal as part of the Nalambalam circuit, and others stand in Mathura, Rishikesh and Telangana.
kidSummary: Shatrughna is the youngest brother of Rama, and twin of Lakshmana. His name means 'one who stops enemies'. In the stories he looks after Ayodhya while his brothers are away, and later he helps people by defeating a dangerous king named Lavana. The city of Mathura is linked with him.

story.title: Twins in the palace
story.text: Shatrughna was born with his twin Lakshmana to Queen Sumitra. Their father had prayed for sons with a special sacrifice and a sweet pudding.

story.title: A big wedding
story.text: When the four brothers were grown, they were married on the same occasion to four sisters from Mithila. Shatrughna's wife was Shrutakirti.

story.title: A quiet job
story.text: While Rama was in the forest and Bharata lived at Nandigrama, Shatrughna stayed in Ayodhya. He looked after the daily running of the kingdom and comforted the queens.

story.title: A request to Rama
story.text: Later, sages asked for help against Lavana, a king who troubled them. Shatrughna asked Rama if he could go instead of anyone else.

story.title: The forest of honey
story.text: Shatrughna set out for Madhuvana, the forest of honey, where Lavana ruled the city of Madhupura.

story.title: A new city
story.text: In the Ramayana he defeated Lavana with a special arrow, and then ruled the region. Many people say this is how the city of Mathura came about.

facts.text: While Rama was exiled, Shatrughna once seized the maid Manthara and wanted to punish her. Bharata stopped him, saying Rama would not approve.
Madhuvana, the forest of honey, grew into Madhupura and then Mathura. A plaque in the Mathura Museum credits Shatrughna with taking the land.
On his way to Madhupura, Shatrughna was a guest at Valmiki's hermitage the very night Sita's twins were born. He heard the news there and left at dawn.

Before the Lavana mission Rama gave Shatrughna a celestial arrow made long ago in Vishnu's own form against Madhu and Kaitabha. Rama had not used it on Ravana because it would have destroyed too many beings.
At the gate of Madhupura, Lavana struck Shatrughna down with a tree and, thinking him dead, went to gather food instead of fetching his trident. Shatrughna rose and took his place again.
When Shatrughna lifted the celestial arrow, its blaze alarmed the whole universe. The gods ran to Brahma, who explained it was Vishnu's own primeval form, made to end Lavana.
In the Thai Ramakien, Phra Satarut, the Shatrughna figure, is a manifestation of the god Narai's mace, not the discus that Indian tradition links to him.

On his way home from Madhupura, Shatrughna stayed at Valmiki's hermitage and heard Rama's story sung there. He wept, and when his soldiers wondered if they were dreaming he told them not to question the sage.

After Lavana fell, the gods agreed the city would be called Shurasena. Valmiki likens the capital to a crescent moon on the Yamuna, and Shatrughna had Lavana's grand buildings painted in many colours.
Shatrughna's Payyammal temple is the last stop of Kerala's Nalambalam pilgrimage, the smallest of the four with the smallest idol, which suits the brother often called the least known.
Sri Kalyana Ramachandra Sannadhi in Medak, Telangana, honours Shatrughna and Shrutakirti and is said to be the only temple in India with statues of all of Rama's brothers and their wives.

quiz.why: Shatrughna and Lakshmana were both born to Sumitra.

quiz.q: Which city is linked to Shatrughna's victory over Lavana?
quiz.why: Many tellings say Mathura grew from Madhupura after he defeated Lavana.
It combines words for enemy and killing.
He married Shrutakirti, as part of the four-brother wedding.

quiz.q: When Lavana struck Shatrughna down and went off to find food, what did he fail to fetch?
quiz.why: He thought Shatrughna was dead and went for food instead of fetching his trident, so Shatrughna rose and fought on.
